title: Connection fidelity prober: tokenflow tracing + p95 regression gates for SSE/WebSocket
creator: Asha Nair
description:
Purpose: build a high-fidelity connection & tokenflow prober for streaming chat (SSE + WebSocket) that prioritizes end-to-end fidelity (connection churn, TLS handshake, reconnects), accurate token/sec accounting, and automated p95 regression detection for CI and long-running benchmarks.

Scope: generator and verifier components that: (1) simulate session distributions (short QA, multi-turn chat, long generative sessions), (2) exercise KV cache priming and prefix reuse, (3) model realistic token pacing and backpressure, (4) capture per-session token timeline traces for p95 and token/sec computation, and (5) run continuous regression detection against a baseline.

Acceptance criteria:
- Harness can sustain configurable sustained tokens/sec target (example 250k tokens/sec aggregate) across mixed session types with configurable multiplexing factor.
- Accurate per-session and aggregate metrics: tokens/sec, p50/p90/p95/p99 latency (generation time per token and first-byte), connection error rate, reconnect frequency, and KV cache hit ratio.
- Regression gate: automated daily job that compares p95 and error-rate deltas using a statistically robust sliding-window test (bootstrap + 95% CI) and opens an alert if p95 increases > 15% and is statistically significant.
- Integrations: dashboard in Grafana, alerts to #infra-slo and PagerDuty for P0 regressions, and GitHub PR status check that can fail on regression for release branches.

Design decisions & trade-offs:
- We will implement tokenflow tracing by instrumenting the client library to emit per-token timestamps and sequence IDs to a local time-series sink; this trades slightly higher agent overhead for precise p95 attribution. Overhead will be measured and capped at <2% CPU per load agent.
- Use multiplexed connections to emulate real clients (HTTP/1.1 SSE and WS multiplexed per-agent) rather than spinning up thousands of full OS TCP connections to keep test infra cost manageable. We will still include a separate churn mode that opens/tears-down connections to emulate mobile-app behavior.
- For regression detection, we will use a rolling 7-day baseline and a 24-hour test window. Decision rationale: balances sensitivity to regressions and resistance to transient noise.
- KV cache priming: scenarios will include cold start (no cache), warmed by replaying prefixes, and synthetic warm-up where cache hit-rate is driven to target values.

Implementation notes:
- New harness binary: flux-prober (Go) derived from flux-loadgen but with tokenflow-tracing and an embedded event uploader.
- Storage of traces and aggregates in a dedicated metrics index (Prometheus for aggregates, ClickHouse for tokenflow traces).
- CI integration: a GitHub Action workflow (gha/regression-prober.yml) that can run short smoke suites on PRs and full-day jobs on release branches.

Operational runbook (initial):
1) Start flux-prober on core-load workers with config profile (scenario: mixed-chat-70/20/10, target-agg-tokens=250000).
2) Monitor dashboard: tokenflow->tokens/sec, p95 token latency, connection churn.
3) If automated gate trips: run bisect script (tools/prober/bisect.sh) that narrows to commit ranges and deploy snapshots of runtime-1.22 kernels for verification.

Risks & mitigations:
- Instrumentation overhead skewing results: run A/B with/without tracing on small runs to quantify overhead and compensate.
- Synthetic workloads not representative: we will collect a week of production sampling (sanitized) to seed session-length and token distribution.

Next milestones:
- 2026-02-25: prototype flux-prober v0.1 (single-agent, tokenflow traces).
- 2026-03-05: distributed mode + KV priming scenarios.
- 2026-03-12: CI integration + preliminary dashboard.
- 2026-03-25: regression gate enabled for runtime-1.22 nightly job.
